land.text: Lindsey; Cliopatria's Northumbria shape from 626 holds 17 of its 18 cells

successors.note: Cliopatria's Northumbria shapes of 626-681 contain Lindsey. No opened page says that Northumbria conquered Lindsey in 625-626; the page says Lindsey was 'at times part of Deira, Northumbria, and especially Mercia'.
Mercia took it after the Battle of the Trent in 679 (Cliopatria from 682); 'Lindsey would from then on become a client state of Mercia', absorbed in the 8th century (Lindsey page, no year).

capitals.name: Lindum (Lincoln)
capitals.note: 'It is believed that Roman Lindum (Lincoln) was the capital of Lindsey.' The page names no capital in so many words.

correction.text: unchanged; the shape should run from about 450 (the page: 'from about 450, Lindsey was one of the lesser kingdoms') to 545

keyframe_review.note: The page gives no area, so the Cliopatria figure cannot be checked against it. The page puts the kingdom 'between the Humber estuary and the Wash', with inland boundaries on the Witham, Trent and Foss Dyke and the Isle of Axholme inside it; the shape fits that frame (bounding box 0.8 W-0.3 E, 52.9-53.7 N). Only the years change: Cliopatria starts in 534, the page says 'from about 450'. The page dates nothing else in these years.

The page gives no area, so the Cliopatria figure cannot be checked against it. 3,976 km2 against 3,933 km2 in 534-545: a 43 km2 outline difference, not a border move; no event is behind it. Unverified: page silent.
Back to the 3,933 km2 outline of 534; the same land. The page has nothing dated between about 500 and 625.

3,976 km2, the same land. Cliopatria's Kingdom of Northumbria begins in 612 as Lindsey's northern neighbour; the page says Lindsey was 'at times part of Deira, Northumbria, and especially Mercia' without years.

The last shape, 623-625. 'in 625, Bede recounts, the missionary Paulinus of York was received by the praefectus of Lindum': a prefect, not a king, receives him. The page gives 628 for the same mission on Stenton's reading. From 626 Cliopatria's Northumbria shape contains Lindsey's land (17 of its 18 cells).

region.text: Lindsey, 'between the Humber estuary and the Wash', with the Witham, Trent and Foss Dyke inland and the Isle of Axholme; Cliopatria's first shape

ledger.note: c. 450: Lindsey is one of the lesser Anglo-Saxon kingdoms. 'from about 450, Lindsey was one of the lesser kingdoms'; 'Its subjugation may have occurred around AD 500'. The year is the page's loose date; the land is the page's description of the boundaries and Cliopatria's shape.

625: Lindsey's last year in Cliopatria; Northumbria's shape holds its land from 626. No opened page dates the end of the kingdom: the page says only that Lindsey was 'at times part of Deira, Northumbria, and especially Mercia', that Paulinus was received by the praefectus of Lindum in 625, and that it was 'absorbed into Mercia in the 8th century'. The Wulfhere page has Ecgfrith of Northumbria forcing Wulfhere to give up Lindsey in 674 and the Trent page makes it a Mercian client state after the battle of 679 (see the Mercia ledger).

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line; the boundaries on the Witham, Trent, Foss Dyke and the Isle of Axholme are the page's description of a frontier, not a dated line.

sources.title: Kingdom of Lindsey
sources.note: Identity, boundaries, Lincoln, c. 450, the 625 Paulinus sentence. A short page: no infobox, no area, no kings with dates, no account of the conquest (asked twice, one page).

sources.title: Lindisfaras
sources.note: Thin: the page is about the name Lindisfarne; nothing on the kingdom's history. Nothing from it is used.

sources.title: Mercia
sources.note: Infobox 'Preceded by: Kingdom of Lindsey'; the 679 Trent sentence.

sources.title: Battle of the Trent
sources.note: 679, Lindsey a client state of Mercia afterwards. Thin on the transfers.

sources.title: Wulfhere of Mercia
sources.note: Wulfhere surrenders Lindsey to Ecgfrith (674); Æthelred recovers it a few years after his accession.

notes: No wars are listed: none is dated inside 450-625 on the pages opened. The Battle of the Trent (674-679, Lindsey the prize) is in the Mercia dossier. Lindsey page is short (no infobox, no dated list of kings, no conquest narrative) and the Lindisfaras page redirects to the Lindisfarne name article: five pages opened (budget 5), most of the dated material comes from the Mercia, Trent and Wulfhere pages and concerns Lindsey after Cliopatria's last shape. Start 450 is the page's 'from about 450'; Cliopatria starts in 534. End 625 is Cliopatria's year (confidence 1): the opened pages do not date the end of Lindsey's own kingship. The kingdom may have lasted as a subject kingdom: Wulfhere held it until Ecgfrith's victory (674, or 661 on the Mercian Supremacy page), Mercia took it back in 679 and kept it as a 'client state', absorbed in the 8th century; a gap-filler with the Bede/Tribal Hidage pages (Edwin's conquest, Paulinus and Blecca, 628) could extend the dossier with vassal tints. Cliopatria draws Lindsey inside Northumbria 626-681, inside Mercia 682-865, split between Mercia (12 cells) and the Viking settlements shape (6 cells) in 866-869, inside the Viking settlements shape 870-877 and inside the Danelaw shape from 878. The Mercia dossier carries the events from 661 on (contest 674-679, gain 679, loss 866). Kings: the page mentions Aldfrith (Aldfrið) and the Anglian collection of genealogies made late in Offa's reign; no reign years, so no ruler strip. Regions: Cliopatria's own shape only; 'Lindsey' as a region name is not in the gazetteer but is not needed.
